jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About XDOF

XDOF is the data engine for embodied intelligence. We help the world's leading robotics and foundation-model labs unlock general-purpose robots by delivering the highest-quality teleoperation, on-embodiment, and egocentric data and paired with our own hardware ecosystem and a model fine-tuning loop that closes the loop on data quality. We recently emerged from stealth and are scaling our customer base of frontier AI and humanoid companies quickly.

About the role

We're hiring our founding Forward Deployed Engineers. You'll embed with our most strategic customers and own their success end-to-end, from translating their model and data needs into concrete collection / annotation / delivery specs, to making sure the data we ship actually moves their model performance.

This is a critical role that today, our founders and core engineers absorb directly. As an FDE, you'll be the single technical owner for a portfolio of accounts, sitting at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development, and you'll help define our forward-deployed motion as we grow.

What you'll do

  • Own end-to-end delivery for a set of strategic customers: scope requirements, sequence delivery, QA before shipping, and clear blockers.

  • Be the first technical responder for your accounts: triage questions, manage expectations on timelines and on still-maturing data products, and escalate only what genuinely needs it.

  • Represent XDOF's technical depth to sophisticated customers while protecting proprietary methodology

  • Close the loop: turn recurring customer needs and delivery pain into concrete input for our data-engine, pipeline, and annotation roadmaps, and codify what works into reusable playbooks.

  • Grow the motion: as the role matures, lead platform-integration engagements and model fine-tuning / evaluation services for enterprise customers.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years of engineering experience, ideally including customer-facing or forward-deployed work.

  • Founding-engineer profile, strongly preferred: you've owned many things at once and solved hard problems without a playbook, and you want to talk to customers.

  • Strong production coding (Python preferred), with real experience shipping and operating data pipelines or infrastructure.

  • High agency and comfort with ambiguity: you drive customer outcomes rather than wait for a spec.

  • Excellent communication and low ego: you can run discovery, push back respectfully on unrealistic asks, and explain hard tradeoffs to both engineers and executives.

Nice to have

  • Background in robotics, embodied AI, autonomy, or ML data infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with robot-learning data (teleoperation, egocentric, VLA / robot foundation models) and formats like MCAP, HDF5, etc.

  • Forward-deployed or solutions experience at an enterprise or frontier-AI company.

jobs.title: LATAM Operations Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Role Mission
Own the build-out of XDOF’s ground-level data acquisition operation in LATAM (Mexico/Brazil), taking the region to a fully operating, self-auditing local network. This role owns the end-to-end pipeline of securing high-fidelity physical-world data (Egocentric, Teleoperation, etc.) — from signing individual high-value venues to institutionalizing multi-scenario local partnerships.

Location：
Based in Mexico or Brazil.

Responsibilities

  • Data collection scene expansion: Own the ground-level expansion strategy and 0-1 execution to build an expanding pipeline of robotics data collection - developing and closing a diversified network of data collection venues and access points (retail, logistics, industrial, urban, etc.)

  • Team Building & Management: Recruit, train, and manage data collection execution teams. Establish SOPs to ensure data integrity and operational velocity.

  • Efficiency Optimization: Monitor offline operational data to optimize workflows and staffing, controlling cost per usable hour while maximizing output.

  • Hardware management: manage the deployment, maintenance and calibration of multi-modal data collection hardware.

  • Operational Optimization and Feedback: Monitor offline operational data to optimize workflows and staffing, provide clear operational feedback to central teams; document market learnings as SOPs/playbooks for reuse in future markets.


Qualifications

  • 3–5+ years of experience managing field operations, growth, or ground execution for major tech platforms, IoT companies, or hardware-enabled startups.

  • Proven track record of sourcing, onboarding, and managing SME partnerships and vendor networks (Required).

  • Working proficiency or fluency in Spanish, Portuguese, or other target-market languages is highly preferred.

  • Solid grasp of Embodied AI and machine learning data fundamentals (e.g., Teleoperation workflows, Egocentric/First-Person vision requirements) with the ability to translate technical data specifications into field operational blueprints.

  • A resilient, "builder" mindset with a high tolerance for ambiguity, comfortable traveling frequently and executing directly in unstructured or high-friction environments.

  • Strong cross-functional capability, matching analytical funnel management (SQL/Excel, conversion rates) with high-stakes, face-to-face field negotiation.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Robotics
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At XDOF, we're at an inflection point. Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots, and high-quality training data is the bottleneck. We're building the foundation behind the foundation models – the data collection systems, operational capability, exabyte-scale data warehouse, and software toolchain – to help our partners drive the field forward.

As a Research Engineer at XDOF, you will design, build, and deploy real world robot learning systems, working across manipulation, locomotion, and control to push robots from raw hardware to fully functional systems.

This is a deeply hands on role. You will own systems end to end, from simulation and model training to deployment on real robots, and you will help define the technical foundations that enable large scale robot learning.


Baseline skills:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field

  • Strong experience with Python and modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX

  • Full stack experience across robot learning, including data processing, model training, and deployment

  • Experience designing, implementing, and deploying robot learning systems in research or production environments

  • Strong understanding of both classical robotics techniques and learning based approaches, and the trade offs between them


You might be a good fit if you:

  • Can take a robotics system from 0 to 1 and iterate quickly based on real world feedback

  • Have hands on experience in one or more of the following areas: robot manipulation, locomotion, navigation algorithms, imitation learning, generative modeling, and/or reinforcement learning

  • Are comfortable working across simulation and real hardware, including high degrees of freedom manipulators and mobile robots

  • Are obsessed with state of the art techniques, tools, and research, and enjoy pushing systems beyond what already exists

  • Thrive in fast paced, ambiguous environments where solutions are not predefined

  • Are mission driven and passionate about robotics: work at XDOF is fast paced and constant. We hope you love what you're going to be doing, because you'll be doing a lot of it.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Product Manager

At XDOF, we’re at an inflection point. Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots, and high-quality training data is the bottleneck. We’re building the foundation behind the foundation models – the data collection systems, operational capability, exabyte-scale data warehouse, and software toolchain – to help our partners drive the field forward.

We operate across the US, Shenzhen, and Jakarta, and we’re moving fast on several fronts at once. We’re looking for a Product Manager to be the connective tissue: someone who ships directly with our US engineers, bridges our China and US teams, and owns delivery so work stays on track from the first customer conversation to the final dataset. If you have sharp product sense, a talent for bringing order to messy work, and you’re fluent in both Chinese and English, this role was built for you.

What You’ll Do

This person is the bridge between our offices and the owner of how work actually gets delivered. In practice, you’ll:

  • partner with US engineers, working in-timezone and shipping product directly alongside them

  • own product features end-to-end across different product lines – for example, building out the teleop/XMI product line

  • serve as the CN ↔ EN bridge between the US and China teams, translating context and intent, not just language

  • own customer delivery end-to-end as the DRI, from BD handoff through final data delivery

  • run the team’s operating cadence – standups, OKR check-ins, Linear hygiene – and keep work visible and searchable

  • bring structure to fast-moving, cross-geo tracking so nothing falls through the cracks between offices

About You

Baseline:

  • a proven PM with real product sense who ships directly with engineers

  • native or near-native fluency in both Chinese and English

  • a strong organizer who can impose structure on ambiguous, fast-moving work

  • 2+ years of relevant work experience

  • comfortable operating in 0→1 environments where the process doesn’t exist yet

You might be a good fit if you:

  • have worked in robotics, AI, or another deep-tech, data-heavy domain

  • have coordinated across time zones or distributed, multilingual teams

  • are fluent with modern project-tracking tools (Linear or similar) and like making work legible

  • have owned program management end-to-end, not just one stage of a pipeline

  • are mission-driven and energized by a fast pace – work at XDOF is fast and constant, and there’s a lot of it. We hope you love what you’ll be doing, because you’ll be doing a lot of it!

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Vision / Language Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About XDOF

Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots, and the bottleneck isn't compute. It's data. At XDOF, we're building the foundation behind the foundation models: the data collection systems, annotation pipelines, exabyte-scale data infrastructure, and software toolchain that enable our partners to push the field forward.

We're hiring a Research Engineer / Scientist to help lead technical efforts at the intersection of vision-language models and robot learning. You will build systems that turn raw egocentric and teleoperation video into high-signal training data for VLA models, and increasingly, contribute to the models themselves.

Beyond pipelines, you will drive research into what makes robot data useful: discovering new metadata (contact events, affordance labels, implicit reward signals, dynamics priors from video) that unlock capabilities current approaches miss. You'll explore how structured annotations can improve cross-embodiment transfer, automatic curriculum generation, and world models that predict what actually matters for manipulation. The data layer isn't downstream of the research. It is the research.

What You'll Do

  • Design and implement vision-language pipelines for egocentric and teleoperation video: structured captioning, temporal grounding, action-conditioned scene understanding, and semantic annotation at scale

  • Develop and evaluate representations that bridge visual perception, language, and low-level robot action — spanning VLAs, video prediction, and world models

  • Build and improve data curation systems that assess quality, diversity, and coverage of large-scale robot demonstration datasets

  • Work hands-on with bimanual and high-DoF manipulation data, including real teleoperation footage and sim-generated rollouts

  • Collaborate directly with partner labs to define data requirements and close the loop between data quality and downstream policy performance

  • Stay current on the research frontier (VLAs, video foundation models, flow matching, DiT architectures, egocentric pretraining) and translate insights into production systems

Required:

  • MS or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field from a top-tier program

  • 3–7 years of research or applied research experience (industry or academic) in one or more of: vision-language models, video understanding, robot learning, or generative modeling

  • Deep fluency in PyTorch; working knowledge of large-scale training infrastructure (distributed training, mixed precision, large batch workflows)

  • Published work or demonstrable impact in VLMs/VLAs, video representation learning, imitation learning, or a closely related area

  • Strong engineering fundamentals — you can design clean systems, not just run experiments

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and equity

  • Comprehensive health and wellness benefits

  • Flexible work arrangements

  • Collaborative and fast-paced work environment

  • Opportunity to shape the future of robotics and AI alongside an ambitious, values-driven team

Level: Mid Level to Senior Research Scientist (L4–L5 equivalent) Location: San Mateo

Note: Junior candidates will still be considered

If you’re excited to help build the infrastructure powering tomorrow’s intelligent machines, we’d love to hear from you!

At XDOF, we're building the foundation behind the foundation models: the data collection systems, annotation pipelines, exabyte-scale data infrastructure, and software toolchain that enable our partners to push the field forward.

We're hiring a Research Engineer / Scientist to help lead technical efforts at the intersection of vision-language models and robot learning. You will build systems that turn raw egocentric and teleoperation video into high-signal training data for VLA models, and increasingly, contribute to the models themselves.

Beyond pipelines, you will drive research into what makes robot data useful: discovering new metadata (contact events, affordance labels, implicit reward signals, dynamics priors from video) that unlock capabilities current approaches miss. You'll explore how structured annotations can improve cross-embodiment transfer, automatic curriculum generation, and world models that predict what actually matters for manipulation. The data layer isn't downstream of the research. It is the research.

 - Design and implement vision-language pipelines for egocentric and teleoperation video: structured captioning, temporal grounding, action-conditioned scene understanding, and semantic annotation at scale

 - Develop and evaluate representations that bridge visual perception, language, and low-level robot action — spanning VLAs, video prediction, and world models

 - Build and improve data curation systems that assess quality, diversity, and coverage of large-scale robot demonstration datasets

 - Work hands-on with bimanual and high-DoF manipulation data, including real teleoperation footage and sim-generated rollouts

 - Collaborate directly with partner labs to define data requirements and close the loop between data quality and downstream policy performance

 - MS or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field from a top-tier program

 - 3–7 years of research or applied research experience (industry or academic) in one or more of: vision-language models, video understanding, robot learning, or generative modeling

 - Deep fluency in PyTorch; working knowledge of large-scale training infrastructure (distributed training, mixed precision, large batch workflows)

 - Published work or demonstrable impact in VLMs/VLAs, video representation learning, imitation learning, or a closely related area

 - Strong engineering fundamentals — you can design clean systems, not just run experiments




BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation and equity

 - Comprehensive health and wellness benefits

 - Flexible work arrangements

 - Collaborative and fast-paced work environment

 - Opportunity to shape the future of robotics and AI alongside an ambitious, values-driven team

Level: Mid Level to Senior Research Scientist (L4–L5 equivalent) Location: San Mateo 

Note: Junior candidates will still be considered



If you’re excited to help build the infrastructure powering tomorrow’s intelligent machines, we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Robotics Data
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At XDOF, we’re at an inflection point. Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots, and high-quality training data is the bottleneck. We’re building the foundation behind the foundation models – the data collection systems, operational capability, exabyte-scale data warehouse, and software toolchain – to help our partners drive the field forward.

The models are only as good as the data. We’re looking for a Robotics Data Engineer to be the person who knows whether our data is trustworthy, across every modality we collect. You’ll analyze, validate, and build tooling around data from teleoperation on real hardware, egocentric capture, UMI-style grippers, and more. If something is wrong with the data, you’re the first to catch it and the one who helps us fix the process.

What You’ll Do

Robotics data engineers are the bridge between raw collection and usable training data. Sample projects include:

  • analyzing robotics data across modalities to identify quality issues: plotting joint velocities, validating camera poses, checking gripper encoder accuracy, and flagging anomalous collection sessions

  • building automated validation pipelines that run on ingestion and catch problems before data enters the warehouse

  • designing and documenting data formats and schemas across collection modalities, ensuring they are consistent, versioned, and well-understood by partners and internal researchers

  • building data visualization tools and dashboards so the broader team can inspect and understand the data without writing custom scripts

  • validating cross-modal temporal alignment, including timestamp synchronization, dropped frame detection, and clock drift across camera, joint, and gripper streams

  • defining quality metrics and thresholds per modality and tracking whether data quality is improving or degrading as collection scales

  • cataloging edge cases and failure modes into a shared taxonomy so the team has a common language for data issues

  • working closely with data collection operators to trace quality issues back to their root cause, whether systemic (hardware calibration, sensor drift) or operator-specific

About You

Baseline skills:

  • bachelor’s or master’s degree (or equivalent experience) in robotics, computer science, mechanical engineering, or a related field

  • strong Python data skills (numpy, pandas, matplotlib or plotly) and comfort working with large, messy datasets

  • solid understanding of 3D geometry, coordinate frames, and spatial transformations

  • intuition for physical systems: you can look at a trajectory or a joint velocity plot and tell when something is off

  • experience designing or working with structured data formats (protobuf, HDF5, ROS bags, or similar)

You might be a good fit if you:

  • have hands-on experience with robotics data, whether from a research lab, a robotics startup, or a manipulation/locomotion project

  • have worked with teleoperation systems, motion capture, or egocentric data collection

  • have experience with signal processing, sensor fusion, or time-series analysis

  • have built internal data visualization tools or dashboards for technical teams

  • have worked on data versioning, lineage tracking, or schema migration in a production setting

  • are very comfortable working in 0→1 environments

  • are mission-driven and passionate about robotics: work at XDOF is fast-paced and constant. We hope you love what you’re going to be doing, because you’ll be doing a lot of it!

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Perception
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At XDOF, we’re at an inflection point. Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots, and high-quality training data is the bottleneck. We’re building the foundation behind the foundation models – the data collection systems, operational capability, exabyte-scale data warehouse, and software toolchain – to help our partners drive the field forward.

The Perception Algorithm team transforms raw multimodal sensor data into high-quality robot training annotations. You will be deeply involved in the complete loop from data collection to model delivery — sensor calibration, SLAM localization, human pose estimation, perception model training, and embedded deployment. Your work directly determines the quality ceiling of our training data.

Core Responsibilities

Human Pose Estimation

  • Design and optimize hand pose estimation pipelines supporting accurate joint angle extraction from teleoperation data collection

  • Build full-body pose estimation systems for motion capture and teleoperation action annotation ground truth generation

  • Research and apply vision-based pose estimation methods (markerless) to reduce data collection costs

  • Retargeting pose estimation outputs with robot joint angle data to generate consistent training annotations

Robot Perception & Calibration

  • Design and maintain intrinsic/extrinsic calibration pipelines for multi-camera arrays (factory calibration + online recalibration)

  • Build visual SLAM / V-SLAM systems supporting real-time localization and scene reconstruction on data collection platforms

  • Implement hand-eye calibration between cameras and robot end-effectors

  • Develop temporal alignment solutions across multimodal sensors (cameras, IMU, data gloves, force sensors)

Perception Model Training & Deployment

  • Train and iterate on perception models including object detection, instance segmentation, and 6DoF pose estimation

  • Optimize model inference using TensorRT / CUDA for real-time performance on robot embedded platforms

  • Write custom CUDA kernels for low-level acceleration of perception tasks

  • Design evaluation metric frameworks for perception models; continuously track the relationship between model performance and data quality

End-to-End Loop from Data Collection to Model Delivery

  • Contribute to the design of automated annotation pipelines that convert sensor data into structured training labels

  • Build Auto QA modules to filter low-quality data including anomalous frames, failed demonstrations, and sensor dropouts

  • Collaborate with ML engineers and data infrastructure teams to ensure perception output formats meet downstream VLA model training requirements

  • Establish feedback mechanisms linking perception accuracy to model training outcomes, continuously improving annotation quality

Requirements

Must-Have

  • 5+ years of industry experience in robot perception or computer vision

  • Strong 3D vision fundamentals: stereo and structured-light camera principles, 3D reconstruction

  • Proficiency with SLAM frameworks (ORB-SLAM, VINS-Mono, FastLIO, etc.) or V-SLAM system development experience

  • Hands-on engineering experience with human pose estimation: hand joints (MediaPipe, MANO) or full-body pose (OpenPose, SMPLify, etc.)

  • Proficient in deep learning training frameworks for perception model training, tuning, and evaluation

  • TensorRT deployment experience with real-time inference optimization on embedded platforms (Jetson, Horizon, etc.)

  • CUDA programming fundamentals; ability to write or debug custom kernels

  • Proficient in C++ and Python with ROS / ROS2 development experience

  • Proficient with AI coding agents

Nice to Have

  • Engineering experience with 6DoF object pose estimation (FoundPose, FoundationPose, GDR-Net, etc.)

  • Familiarity with 3D Gaussian Splatting or NeRF for scene reconstruction or data augmentation

  • Experience with robot manipulation or teleoperation systems

  • End-to-end development experience with automated annotation pipelines or ground truth generation systems

  • Published research in perception, pose estimation, or robotics

What We Offer

  • Direct involvement in the most critical technical challenge in embodied intelligence: producing high-quality robot training data

  • An environment working alongside top-tier robotics engineers and ML researchers

  • Proprietary hardware platforms (humanoid robots, camera arrays, data gloves)

  • A fast-paced, high-autonomy 0→1 work environment

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Robotics Control (Whole Body Control)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At XDOF, we're at an inflection point. Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots, and high-quality training data is the bottleneck. We're building the foundation behind the foundation models — the data collection systems, operational capability, exabyte-scale data warehouse, and software toolchain — to help our partners drive the field forward.

Great data starts with great hardware behavior. We're looking for a Robotics Controls Engineer to build the high-performance control systems that make our dexterous manipulators and humanoid robots move safely, precisely, and repeatably — because every teleoperation session, every collection run, and every downstream model depends on robots that respond exactly as commanded.

What You'll Do

Controls engineers are the bridge between robot hardware and reliable, high-quality motion. Sample projects include:

  • implementing joint-space and Cartesian impedance / torque control for 7+ DoF robotic arms

  • building whole-body control (WBC) for highly redundant humanoids with mobile bases, arms, and actuated torsos

  • designing optimization-based controllers: QP formulations, inverse dynamics, task/null-space control, and redundancy resolution

  • developing collision-aware motion and control, including self-collision avoidance and environment constraints

  • implementing and integrating real-time control software on physical robots, from simulation through hardware deployment

  • tuning and validating controller performance across diverse manipulation and locomotion tasks

  • working closely with data collection operators and hardware teams to diagnose and resolve control-related failure modes during teleoperation and autonomous runs

About You

Baseline skills:

  • bachelor's or master's degree (or equivalent experience) in robotics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field

  • strong fundamentals in robot dynamics, kinematics, and feedback control

  • hands-on experience implementing controllers on real robotic systems, not just in simulation

  • strong C++ and/or Python, and comfort working with real-time robotics systems

You might be a good fit if you:

  • have experience with whole-body control, operational-space control, MPC, or optimization-based control

  • come from a background in humanoid robotics, manipulation, legged robotics, or advanced industrial robot control

  • have worked on real-time embedded control software and understand the constraints of deploying to physical hardware

  • are very comfortable working in 0→1 environments

  • are mission-driven and passionate about robotics: work at XDOF is fast-paced and constant. We hope you love what you're going to be doing, because you'll be doing a lot of it!

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Research Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Research Engineer

At XDOF, we’re at an inflection point. Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots, and high-quality training data is the bottleneck. We’re building the foundation behind the foundation models – the data collection systems, operational capability, exabyte-scale data warehouse, and software toolchain – to help our partners drive the field forward.

Our research teams move fast and produce breakthrough work, but research code and production code are different things. We’re looking for a Research Engineer to bridge that gap: someone who can read a research prototype, understand it deeply, and turn it into something that runs reliably at scale on real hardware. You can expect to float across teams to wherever the highest-priority needs are, across perception, ML, and data infrastructure.

What You’ll Do

Research engineers take prototype code and make it production-grade. Sample projects include:

  • taking a research perception pipeline (pose estimation, SLAM, calibration) and hardening it for reliable, real-time execution on embedded platforms

  • profiling and optimizing performance-critical code at the CPU, memory, and GPU level using tools like perf, NSight, and custom microbenchmarks

  • writing and debugging CUDA kernels for low-level acceleration of compute-heavy workloads

  • integrating research outputs into the production codebase with proper testing, error handling, and observability

  • containerizing and packaging workloads (Docker) so they can be scaled and deployed by the infrastructure team

  • understanding and leveraging the infrastructure team’s orchestration and compute systems to hand off production-ready workloads cleanly

  • working with researchers to understand algorithmic intent and make informed tradeoffs between accuracy, latency, and resource usage

About You

Baseline skills:

  • 3+ years of industry experience in software engineering with a focus on systems, performance, or production ML

  • strong C++ proficiency, including modern C++ (C++17/20), memory management, and performance-conscious coding patterns

  • CUDA programming experience: ability to write, profile, and debug GPU kernels

  • experience with CPU performance optimization: profiling, cache behavior, SIMD, latency reduction

  • proficiency with Python and familiarity with ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) at the level needed to read and modify research code

  • comfort with Linux systems, including build systems, debugging tools, and containerization

You might be a good fit if you:

  • have taken research or prototype code and shipped it in a production system

  • have worked on real-time or embedded systems where latency and resource constraints matter

  • have experience with perception, computer vision, or robotics systems

  • have optimized model inference for deployment (TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, or similar)

  • understand the full lifecycle from research notebook to containerized, monitored production service

  • are very comfortable working in 0→1 environments

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About XDOF

XDOF builds the data and operational infrastructure behind the next generation of robotics and AI. We help frontier labs and the entire robotics ecosystem develop general-purpose robots through scalable data collection, software, hardware, and operations.

The role

We're hiring our founding Marketing Lead to own how XDOF shows up in the world to customers, to partners, and to future teammates. You’ll run major product launches, own our major marketing channels and curate our presence at events and conferences.

Our industry faces many unsolved challenges on its way to building general-purpose robots. Our customers are varied in their research directions and product applications. XDOF is their first call for all things data and infrastructure, and you’d have a unique opportunity to drive marketing for all the different ways we serve them. In one instance, you may be driving a product launch for an upcoming service that only XDOF can do. In another, you may be owning a technical report in partnership with our academic collaborators. No matter the project, your work is informed by taste, sophistication and ambition - the XDOF way.

What you'll do

  • Own marketing end to end: messaging, positioning, content, website, announcements, thought leadership, and the ongoing narrative about XDOF and the robotics industry. Turn a technical, nuanced business into a story that lands with very different audiences.

  • Run our events and field presence: plan and execute XDOF's presence at industry conferences and curated gatherings of our own.

  • Reach our key audiences deliberately: customers, consortium and data partners, and prospective hires. Build a distinct message and engagement strategy for each while keeping one coherent XDOF narrative.

  • Build the foundation: set up the tools, cadences, and early processes a growing marketing function will need, and lay the groundwork for the team that follows.

What we're looking for

  • Strong comms background. You write clearly and persuasively, you can find the through-line in a complex story, and you've owned messaging and content for a company or brand before.

  • Comfort with technical and B2B subject matter. You can get fluent fast in robotics and AI, and translate between deeply technical people and the outside world.

  • Real events experience. You've planned and run events, managed the logistics without drama, and know how to turn a conference or a dinner into pipeline and relationships.

  • A head for strategy. You don't just execute briefs; you have opinions about positioning, audience, and timing, and you can make the case for them. This is the differentiator we care about most.

  • Range across audiences. You can shift register between a frontier AI lab, a large industrial partner, and a candidate without losing the thread.

  • A builder's temperament. Self-directed, comfortable with ambiguity, and energized by being early. You'd rather define the function than inherit one.

Nice to have

  • Experience in AI, robotics, deep tech, data, or enterprise/B2B marketing.

  • Startup or early-stage experience, especially as a first or early marketing hire.

  • An existing network in the AI or robotics ecosystem.

  • Familiarity with bringing a genuinely new offering to market.

Why XDOF

  • Shape an industry. The work we do literally defines standards in robotics and enables new possibilities.

  • Real ownership. First marketing hire, direct line to the founders, and the mandate to build marketing your way.

  • A seat at the center. XDOF sits between the frontier labs and the physical world. You'll have a rare vantage point on the future of physical AI before anyone else does.


XDOF is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are committed to building a team that reflects a range of perspectives and experiences.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Robotics Infrastructure
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At XDOF, we’re at an inflection point. Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots, and high-quality training data is the bottleneck. We’re building the foundation behind the foundation models – the data collection systems, operational capability, exabyte-scale data warehouse, and software toolchain – to help our partners drive the field forward.

We’re looking for a Robotics Infrastructure Engineer to build the product and infrastructure that lets us and our partners deploy and evaluate learned robotis policies on real hardware. Examples of things you might work on are: deploying VLAs, imitation learning models, and DAgger workflows onto embodied systems, building the evaluation frameworks that measure how they perform, and shipping the product surfaces that make this accessible to partners.

What You’ll Do

Robotics Infrastructure engineers own the systems that get models running on robots and measure how well they work. Sample projects include:

  • deploying and running learned robot policies (VLAs, imitation learning, DAgger) on real hardware, including inference setup, on-robot tuning, and failure diagnosis

  • designing and building evaluation frameworks that benchmark policy performance on physical robots, with metric definition, result aggregation, and partner-facing reporting

  • building the product that lets partners configure, launch, and monitor evaluation runs and model deployments

  • building orchestration systems that schedule evaluation runs and model deployments across robot stations

  • integrating LLMs and foundation models into robot workflows for task specification, error recovery, or high-level planning

  • containerizing and packaging robot-side software stacks so new stations and deployments can be brought online quickly and consistently

  • bridging on-robot systems with cloud-side compute, storage, and orchestration

About You

Baseline skills:

  • bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field

  • 3+ years of industry experience in software engineering, with exposure to robotics or ML deployment

  • strong Python skills and comfort working in Linux environments

  • experience deploying ML models to real systems, not just training them

  • familiarity with containerization (Docker) and building reproducible deployment workflows

You might be a good fit if you:

  • have deployed imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or VLA policies on physical robots

  • have built evaluation or benchmarking infrastructure for robotic systems or ML models

  • have experience with DAgger or other interactive data collection and policy refinement loops

  • have experience with ROS/ROS2 and understand robotics middleware at the integration level

  • have built product features or partner-facing tools on top of technical infrastructure

  • are very comfortable working in 0→1 environments

  • are mission-driven and passionate about robotics: work at XDOF is fast-paced and constant. We hope you love what you’re going to be doing, because you’ll be doing a lot of it!

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Vision/Language Research
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots, and the bottleneck isn't compute. It's data. At xdof, we're building the foundation behind the foundation models: the data collection systems, annotation pipelines, exabyte-scale data infrastructure, and software toolchain that enable our partners to push the field forward.

We're hiring a Research Scientist to lead technical efforts at the intersection of vision-language models and robot learning. You will lead an exploratory project on what data a model actually needs in order to reason about and act in the physical world. This is an open question across the field, and the role is largely about finding the answer: studying how frontier models currently fail at embodied tasks, forming hypotheses about which kinds of structured annotations on egocentric video would close those gaps, prototyping them on our data, and running experiments that show whether they help.

The ideal candidate has a research background in representation learning, and some of the following: vision, robotics, and language models.

 
 

What You'll Do

  • Develop and evaluate representations that bridge visual perception, language, and low-level robot action conditioned on different modalities Collaborate directly with partner labs to define data requirements and close the loop between data quality and downstream policy performance

  • Stay current on the research frontier (VLAs, video foundation models, flow matching, DiT architectures, egocentric pretraining) and translate insights into new research and production systems

 
 

About You

Required:

  • PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field from a top-tier program

  • 3–7 years of research or applied research experience (industry or academic) in one or more of: vision-language models, video understanding, robot learning, or generative modeling

  • Deep fluency in PyTorch; working knowledge of large-scale training infrastructure (distributed training, mixed precision, large batch workflows)

  • Published work or demonstrable impact in VLMs/VLAs, video representation learning, imitation learning, or a closely related area

  • Strong engineering fundamentals — you can design clean systems, not just run experiments
